 Meeting Date: May 25, 2023      Convened: 6:35pm                Adjourned: 8:00pm

 TRN – Kimberly Smith                            PBW – Shahad Mohammed


Discussion Items:
The Department of Public Works introduced their staff and provided an overview of the meeting
topics. They provided background information on both departments’ different and overlapping
projects responsibilities, background information on scoring methodology for the Bond Program
and the 20 points for Equity and Overlays, and a recap from the previous meeting on the
Department of Public Works’ specific responsibilities. Then, they went over Public Works’ project
categories and their definitions with picture examples. Afterwards, they covered the Technical
Criteria for scoring all of Public Works’ project categories and the scoring methodology.


The Department of Transportation continued the presentation by introducing their team and going
over Transportation Plan and Policy Guidance, which included the Connect Dallas Strategic
Mobility Plan. To conclude the presentation portion of the meeting, they covered the
Transportation project categories with example pictures, and their Technical Criteria for scoring
projects.
 At the end of the meeting, both departments went over next steps and suggested adding another
meeting in July to cover all the project categories in the Needs Inventory. They then opened the
Questions and Answers session together and addressed the following questions.
Questions:

   •   How is the Needs Inventory updated?
   •   What is the oldest project in the Needs Inventory list?
   •   For the June 13 meeting, will there be sufficient time to present all projects and have
       questions in an hour and a half meeting?
   •   Are they voting as a group or individually when selecting projects?
   •   Is it possible to have federal funds rather than City?
   •   Is it possible to not fund Partnership Projects?
   •   How does the City determine how many points 311 service requests get to the overlay
       score.
   •   How to add a project as a Residents to the Needs inventory
   •   How to find the maps to be used for the Overlay points?
   •   District 10 would like to know how soon they can have a copy of the last meeting’s
       presentation.
Staff stayed after the meeting was adjourned to answer questions. The meeting concluded at 8:00
p.m.
Action Items:

   •   Have the presentation for the next meeting ready and provide to the Subcommittee 4-5
       days in advance
   •   Confirm if it is allowed by the Bond office and City Attorney to add another meeting in July
   •   Send out the Field Trip details
   •   Send out previous and current meeting presentation slides
   •   Send out links to the Needs Inventory and useful maps
   •   Send out definitions for the Public Works technical criteria factors
   •   Send out information on High Crime Areas.

Discussion Items:
The Department of Public Works introduced their staff and provided an overview of the meeting
topics. They provided background information on both departments’ different and overlapping
projects responsibilities, background information on scoring methodology for the Bond Program
and the 20 points for Equity and Overlays, and a recap from the previous meeting on the
Department of Public Works’ specific responsibilities. Then, they went over Public Works’ project
categories and their definitions with picture examples. Afterwards, they covered the Technical
Criteria for scoring all of Public Works’ project categories and the scoring methodology.


The Department of Transportation continued the presentation by introducing their team and going
over Transportation Plan and Policy Guidance, which included the Connect Dallas Strategic
Mobility Plan. To conclude the presentation portion of the meeting, they covered the
Transportation project categories with example pictures, and their Technical Criteria for scoring
projects.

meeting in July to cover all the project categories in the Needs Inventory. They then opened the

Discussion Items:
The Department of Public Works (PBW) introduced their staff and started the presentation
by defining the Needs Inventory, explaining criteria for projects to be placed on the Needs
Inventory list for each asset managed by Public Works, and listing the project categories
that are on the Needs Inventory. Also, PBW presented the overall City Needs per asset
and their percentages along with a detailed data presentation of the Needs share per
Council District for each asset. Public Works staff continued with defining Citywide
projects and categories that would be considered as “Citywide” by referencing the April
2023 Memo to Mayor and Members of the City Council, “2024 Bond Program Development
– Definition of “Citywide” Projects” . Then, they presented a Data comparison for Alleys on
the Needs Inventory per Council District as well as improved versus unimproved alleys.
Afterwards, they covered the Sidewalk Master Plan focus areas and the top priority
bridges list on the Needs Inventory. Sidewalks and Bridges priority lists were also
provided. In the end, staff presented several budget scenarios with the proposed
 allocations breakdown per each asset. Finally, staff opened the questions and answers
session and answered Subcommittee Members’ questions below.

   •   What is the time frame for improvements funded through federal funds?
   •   How are thoroughfares classified?
   •   Are traffic lights part of street improvements?
   •   How often is the Needs Inventory List updated/reclassified?
   •   How is funding divided between unimproved and improved alleys?
   •   Why there is a disproportion for alley improvements per district?
   •   How is the funding mechanism per council district to ensure equity based on
       Needs?
   •   How do you know if districts with higher percentage in Needs will also have higher
       number of higher score projects?
   •   Is the bridges maintenance based on safety issue or cosmetics concern?
   •   How are sidewalk projects identified in the arts district?
   •   Will the funding remaining from 2017 Bond Program be reprogramed for 2024
       Bond?

ance?

bodies.name: Dallas 2024 Community Bond Task Force (Community Bond Task Force / 2024 Bond Task Force)

A.rationale: Official minutes (dallas-cbtf-aug15, hosted on dallascityhall.com under Bond and Construction Management) head the meeting 'Community Bond Task Force / 2024 Bond Task Force,' convened 6:30 p.m. and adjourned 8:48 p.m. on August 15, 2023, and repeatedly identify the body as the CBTF ('Staff briefed the Community Bond Task Force (CBTF)...', 'CBTF received public comment', 'next CBTF meeting'), establishing the convened body as Dallas's 2024 Community Bond Task Force. The Swagit player (provider-player, recording 269608) and chapter data (native-source-chapters) show the identical title and date for the same recording. This is a single convening body, not a joint meeting: the listed staff from Bond and Construction Management and the City Manager's Office, plus the Planning and Urban Design presenter of the ForwardDallas plan, are staff/presenters, not convening bodies, and ForwardDallas is topic content, so no additional bodies are proven. The existing configured feed 'Dallas: 2024 Community Bond Task Force' (dallas-tx-2024-community-bond-task-force) exactly matches this verified body, so publication_action is assign_existing. The 2024 bond subcommittee feeds cover subcommittees rather than the full task force; dallas-tx-2017-citizens-bond-task-force is a different numbered/era body per the identity rule; and the generic dallas-tx-bond-program-meetings family feed is unnecessary because a body-specific feed exists. Transcript garble ('DALLAS TASK FORCE') is voice-to-text error, corrected by the official minutes.

B.rationale: The official August 15, 2023 minutes identify the Community Bond Task Force under the 2024 Bond Task Force heading, record its convening at 6:30 PM, and document its business and adjournment. The provider title and recording-specific chapter corroborate that ownership for recording 269608. Assign the verified proceedings to the dedicated 2024 Community Bond Task Force feed and, under the configured bond-family publication rule, the Bond Program Meetings subscription grouping. The latter is a grouping, not a separate convening body. ForwardDallas was a staff briefing to the task force, not evidence of another body's joint participation. Routine public comment does not warrant Public Info feed membership.
